How an explanation is built

Method, as implemented in explainability.py

Each row of explanations.csv is one routing evaluation by the controller, written at decision time. An explanation is assembled only from values measured or predicted at that moment: the signals for both candidate paths, the forecast for the active path, its interval when one exists, and the projected improvement of switching (signal of the active path minus signal of the candidate).

Feature contributions are not fixed weights. Importance comes from the portable Gradient Boosting artifact itself — split counts across its trees — multiplied by how far this decision's feature values sit from the midpoint of their training ranges. A feature therefore contributes when it is both important to the model and unusual in this sample. When an input is missing (no forecast, no interval, no features), the field is recorded empty, never invented — the completeness counts at the top of this page show exactly how many decisions carry each field.

For the paper, this page is the reproducibility surface for the explainability claim: every aggregate below is recomputed from the recorded CSV files when the page is requested, and the source list names each file used.
